title: Chapter 12: Deploying Your Python AI Agent
content:
Chapter 12: Deploying Your Python AI Agent

Opening Hook: A Local Script Teaches You. A Deployed App Proves You.

A Python script on your laptop is useful.

A deployed AI app is different.

A deployed app can be shown to clients. It can be added to your portfolio. It can be tested by users. It can become a freelance demo. It can become a startup prototype. It can become a real internal tool.

This is the final step in your journey.

In earlier chapters, you built the pieces:

  • LLM calls
  • Prompt templates
  • Command-line assistants
  • RAG
  • Semantic search
  • Tool calling
  • Memory
  • Workflow automation
  • Multi-agent workflows
  • Guardrails
  • Evaluation

Now you will combine those ideas into one capstone project:

Personal AI Work Assistant

This app will include:

  • A web interface
  • General assistant mode
  • Document Q&A mode
  • Tool mode
  • Memory mode
  • Guardrails
  • Evaluation self-check
  • Environment-based secrets
  • README and portfolio documentation
  • Deployment preparation

This chapter is not just about code.

It is about packaging your AI work like a real product.

What You Will Learn

By the end of this chapter, you will understand:

  • How to package a Python AI app
  • How to create a simple Streamlit web interface
  • How to manage secrets safely
  • How to prepare files for deployment
  • How to combine RAG, tools, memory, guardrails, and evaluation
  • How to create a portfolio-ready README
  • How to document limitations honestly
  • How to avoid common deployment mistakes
  • How to present your AI agent professionally

Why This Chapter Matters

A project becomes more valuable when others can use it.

A folder of scripts shows that you practiced.

A deployed app shows that you can build something usable.

For students, this becomes a portfolio project.

For freelancers, this becomes a client demo.

For developers, this becomes proof of practical AI engineering.

For founders, this becomes an MVP prototype.

The goal is not to build a perfect production system in one chapter.

The goal is to build a polished, review-ready, deployable app that demonstrates the skills from this book.

12.1 What Does “Deployment” Mean?

Deployment means making your app available outside your local development environment.

For a beginner AI app, deployment usually includes:

Code repository
↓
Dependencies
↓
Secrets configuration
↓
App entrypoint
↓
Web interface
↓
Hosting platform
↓
Public or private app link

Deployment does not automatically mean your app is production-grade.

Production-grade systems may need authentication, monitoring, rate limits, databases, user isolation, compliance review, and stronger security.

This chapter focuses on a beginner-friendly deployment path.

12.2 Local App vs Deployed App

A local app runs on your machine.

A deployed app runs on a hosted environment.

AreaLocal AppDeployed App
AccessOnly youUsers or clients
Secrets.env filePlatform secrets
DependenciesLocal .venvrequirements.txt
DataLocal filesUploaded or cloud data
DebuggingTerminal logsPlatform logs
RiskLowerHigher
Professional valuePracticePortfolio/demo

Deployment forces you to think more carefully.

If another person can use the app, then you need:

  • Clear setup
  • Safe secrets
  • Error handling
  • User instructions
  • Guardrails
  • Limitations
  • Testing
  • Documentation

12.3 Capstone Project: Personal AI Work Assistant

What This Project Does

The Personal AI Work Assistant is a web app that helps users:

  • Ask general work or study questions
  • Upload and ask questions about documents
  • Summarize text
  • Create task plans
  • Use a calculator tool
  • Save user-approved memory
  • Apply guardrails to risky requests
  • Review output before using it
  • Run a simple self-check evaluation

Who This Helps

This project helps:

  • Students building a portfolio
  • Freelancers creating an AI automation demo
  • Developers learning deployment
  • Professionals building productivity tools
  • Startup founders creating an MVP
  • Business-minded readers packaging AI skills commercially

What You Will Build

12.4 Setup

Step 1: Create the Folder

mkdir chapter_12_capstone
cd chapter_12_capstone
mkdir .streamlit sample_docs outputs

Step 2: Create a Virtual Environment

python -m venv .venv

Activate it.

On macOS or Linux:

source .venv/bin/activate

On Windows PowerShell:

.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

Step 3: Create requirements.txt

openai
streamlit
python-dotenv
pypdf

pytest

Install dependencies:

pip install -r requirements.txt

Step 4: Create .streamlit/secrets.toml.example

OPENAI_API_KEY = "replace_with_your_api_key"
OPENAI_MODEL = "gpt-4.1-mini"
OPENAI_TEMPERATURE = "0.2"

Copy it to .streamlit/secrets.toml.

On macOS or Linux:

cp .streamlit/secrets.toml.example .streamlit/secrets.toml

On Windows PowerShell:

Copy-Item .streamlit/secrets.toml.example .streamlit/secrets.toml

Then edit:

.streamlit/secrets.toml

and add your real API key.

Never commit your real secrets file.

12.5 File: .gitignore

Create .gitignore:

.env
.venv/
__pycache__/
.pytest_cache/
*.pyc
*.log
.streamlit/secrets.toml
outputs/
memory.json

This prevents secrets, local environments, logs, generated outputs, and local memory from being committed.

12.6 File: llm_client.py

This file reads secrets from Streamlit when available, with environment variable fallback.

"""
Capstone LLM client for the Personal AI Work Assistant.
"""

import os from dataclasses import dataclass from dotenv import load_dotenv from openai import OpenAI

load_dotenv()

def read_secret(name: str, default: str | None = None) -> str | None:

"""
Read a secret from Streamlit secrets if available, otherwise from environment variables.

This keeps the app usable locally and in Streamlit deployment.
"""

try:
import streamlit as st

if name in st.secrets:

return str(st.secrets[name])

except Exception:
pass

return os.getenv(name, default)

def read_float_secret(name: str, default: float) -> float:

"""Read a float secret safely."""

raw_value = read_secret(name)

if raw_value is None:
return default

try:

return float(raw_value)

except ValueError:
return default

@dataclass

class LLMConfig:

"""Configuration for the LLM client."""

model: str
temperature: float

class LLMClient:

"""Small reusable LLM client."""

def __init__(self, config: LLMConfig | None = None):
 self.config = config or LLMConfig(
 model=read_secret("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4.1-mini") or "gpt-4.1-mini",
 temperature=read_float_secret("OPENAI_TEMPERATURE", 0.2),
 )

api_key = read_secret("OPENAI_API_KEY")

if not api_key:
raise ValueError(
"OPENAI_API_KEY is missing. Add it to Streamlit secrets or environment variables."
)

self.client = OpenAI(api_key=api_key)

def complete(self, system: str, user: str) -> str:
"""Send a request to the model and return text output."""

if not system.strip():
 raise ValueError("System instruction cannot be empty.")
if not user.strip():
 raise ValueError("User request cannot be empty.")

model_input = f"""
System instruction:

{system.strip()}

User request:

{user.strip()}

"""

response = self.client.responses.create(
model=self.config.model,
input=model_input,
temperature=self.config.temperature,
)

return response.output_text

12.7 File: guardrails.py

This file provides simple reusable guardrails.

"""
Guardrails for the capstone Personal AI Work Assistant.
"""

import re from dataclasses import dataclass, field

@dataclass

class RiskAssessment:

"""Risk assessment result."""

allowed: bool
needs_review: bool
risk_level: str
reason: str
categories: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

SECRET_PATTERNS = [
r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}",
r"api[_-]?key\s*[:=]\s*[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}",
r"password\s*[:=]\s*\S+",
r"token\s*[:=]\s*[A-Za-z0-9_\-\.]{10,}",
]

RISKY_ACTIONS = [
"send email",
"delete",
"purchase",
"transfer money",
"submit",
"post this",
"update database",
"drop table",
]

SENSITIVE_TOPICS = [
"legal advice",
"medical diagnosis",
"investment advice",
"tax advice",
"is this contract safe",
]

def looks_like_secret(text: str) -> bool:

"""Return True if text appears to contain a secret."""

lowered = text.lower()

if any(keyword in lowered for keyword in ["api key", "password", "private key", "secret key"]):
return True

return any(re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE) for pattern in SECRET_PATTERNS)

def assess_request(text: str) -> RiskAssessment:

"""Assess user request risk."""

cleaned = text.strip()

if not cleaned:

return RiskAssessment(

allowed=False,
needs_review=False,
risk_level="low",
reason="Input is empty.",
categories=["empty_input"],
)

if len(cleaned) > 8000:

return RiskAssessment(

allowed=False,
needs_review=True,
risk_level="medium",
reason="Input is too long for this demo.",
categories=["too_long"],
)

categories = []
 lowered = cleaned.lower()

if looks_like_secret(cleaned):
categories.append("possible_secret")

if any(action in lowered for action in RISKY_ACTIONS):
categories.append("risky_action")

if any(topic in lowered for topic in SENSITIVE_TOPICS):
categories.append("sensitive_topic")

if "possible_secret" in categories:

return RiskAssessment(

allowed=False,
needs_review=True,
risk_level="high",
reason="The input appears to contain sensitive information. Do not submit secrets.",
categories=categories,
)

if "risky_action" in categories:

return RiskAssessment(

allowed=True,
needs_review=True,
risk_level="medium",
reason="This request may involve an external or risky action. Draft only; human approval is required.",
categories=categories,
)

if "sensitive_topic" in categories:

return RiskAssessment(

allowed=True,
needs_review=True,
risk_level="medium",
reason="This may involve sensitive professional advice. Use general information only and seek qualified review.",
categories=categories,
)

return RiskAssessment(

allowed=True,
needs_review=False,
risk_level="low",
reason="No obvious risk detected.",
categories=[],
)

def review_message(assessment: RiskAssessment) -> str:

"""Create a human-readable review message."""

if not assessment.needs_review:
return "No special review required."

return f"""
Review required.

Risk level: {assessment.risk_level}
Categories: {', '.join(assessment.categories)}
Reason: {assessment.reason}

Before using this output:
- Review the response manually.
- Do not treat it as professional legal, medical, financial, or tax advice.
- Do not send, delete, purchase, submit, or update anything without approval.
""".strip()

12.8 File: memory_store.py

This file stores user-approved memory locally.

"""
Local memory store for the capstone assistant.
"""

import json from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict from pathlib import Path

MEMORY_FILE = Path("memory.json")

@dataclass

class MemoryItem:

"""One saved memory item."""

id: int
text: str

def default_memory() -> dict:

"""Return default memory structure."""

return {

"next_id": 1,
"items": [],
}

def load_memory(path: Path = MEMORY_FILE) -> dict:

"""Load memory from JSON."""

if not path.exists():

return default_memory()

try:

data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) except json.JSONDecodeError: return default_memory()

if not isinstance(data, dict):

return default_memory()

if "next_id" not in data or "items" not in data:

return default_memory()

return data

def save_memory(data: dict, path: Path = MEMORY_FILE) -> None:

"""Save memory data."""

path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

def add_memory(text: str, path: Path = MEMORY_FILE) -> MemoryItem:

"""Add a user-approved memory item."""

cleaned = text.strip()

if not cleaned:
raise ValueError("Memory cannot be empty.")

if len(cleaned) > 500:
raise ValueError("Memory is too long. Limit: 500 characters.")

data = load_memory(path)
 memory_id = int(data["next_id"])
item = MemoryItem(id=memory_id, text=cleaned)
 data["items"].append(asdict(item))
 data["next_id"] = memory_id + 1

save_memory(data, path)

return item

def list_memory(path: Path = MEMORY_FILE) -> list[MemoryItem]:

"""List saved memory items."""

data = load_memory(path)
 items = []

for raw_item in data.get("items", []):
try:
items.append(
MemoryItem(
id=int(raw_item["id"]),
text=str(raw_item["text"]),
)
)
except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
continue

return items

def clear_memory(path: Path = MEMORY_FILE) -> None:

"""Clear all memory."""

save_memory(default_memory(), path)

def format_memory_for_prompt(path: Path = MEMORY_FILE) -> str:

"""Format memory for prompt context."""

items = list_memory(path)

if not items:
return "No saved memory."

return "\n".join(f"- Memory {item.id}: {item.text}" for item in items)

12.9 File: tools.py

This file contains simple safe tools.

"""
Simple tools for the capstone assistant.
"""

import ast import operator

ALLOWED_OPERATORS = {
ast.Add: operator.add,
ast.Sub: operator.sub,
ast.Mult: operator.mul,
ast.Div: operator.truediv,
ast.Pow: operator.pow,
ast.USub: operator.neg,
ast.UAdd: operator.pos,
}

def evaluate_node(node):

"""Evaluate a safe arithmetic AST node."""

if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, (int, float)):
return node.value

if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
 left = evaluate_node(node.left)
 right = evaluate_node(node.right)
 op_type = type(node.op)

if op_type not in ALLOWED_OPERATORS:
raise ValueError("Unsupported operator.")

return ALLOWED_OPERATORSop_type

if isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp):
 operand = evaluate_node(node.operand)
 op_type = type(node.op)

if op_type not in ALLOWED_OPERATORS:
raise ValueError("Unsupported unary operator.")

return ALLOWED_OPERATORSop_type

raise ValueError("Unsupported expression.")

def calculator(expression: str) -> str:

"""Safely calculate a basic arithmetic expression."""

if not expression.strip():

return "Calculator error: expression cannot be empty."

if len(expression) > 200:

return "Calculator error: expression is too long."

try:
 parsed = ast.parse(expression, mode="eval")
 result = evaluate_node(parsed.body)

return str(result)

except ZeroDivisionError:

return "Calculator error: division by zero."

except Exception as error:

return f"Calculator error: {error}"

def create_task_plan(goal: str) -> str:

"""Create a simple task plan using normal Python logic."""

cleaned = goal.strip()

if not cleaned:

return "Task plan error: goal cannot be empty."

return f"""
Goal:

{cleaned}

Tasks:
1. Clarify the desired outcome.
2. Identify required inputs and resources.
3. Break the work into small steps.
4. Complete the first draft or prototype.
5. Review the result.
6. Improve based on feedback.
7. Prepare final delivery.

Human review:
Required before using this plan for client, legal, financial, or business decisions.
""".strip()

12.10 File: rag_utils.py

This file implements a simple document Q&A helper.

This version uses lightweight keyword-style retrieval so the capstone is easier to deploy. It is still a RAG-style pattern because the assistant retrieves relevant text chunks before generating an answer.

"""
Lightweight RAG utilities for the capstone assistant.

This beginner-friendly implementation uses simple keyword scoring.
For stronger semantic retrieval, adapt Chapter 5's vector database approach.
"""

from io import BytesIO from pypdf import PdfReader

def extract_text_from_pdf_bytes(file_bytes: bytes) -> str:

"""Extract text from uploaded PDF bytes."""

reader = PdfReader(BytesIO(file_bytes))
 page_texts = []

for index, page in enumerate(reader.pages, start=1):
text = page.extract_text() or ""

if text.strip():
page_texts.append(f"[Page {index}]\n{text.strip()}")

if not page_texts:
raise ValueError("No extractable text found. This PDF may be scanned or image-based.")

return "\n\n".join(page_texts)

def chunk_text(text: str, chunk_size: int = 1000, overlap: int = 150) -> list[str]:

"""Split text into overlapping chunks."""

if chunk_size <= 0:
raise ValueError("chunk_size must be greater than 0.")

if overlap < 0 or overlap >= chunk_size:
raise ValueError("overlap must be non-negative and smaller than chunk_size.")

cleaned = " ".join(text.split())

if not cleaned:

return []

chunks = []
 start = 0
while start < len(cleaned):
 end = start + chunk_size
 chunk = cleaned[start:end].strip()

if chunk:
chunks.append(chunk)

start = end - overlap

return chunks

def score_chunk(question: str, chunk: str) -> int:

"""Score a chunk using simple keyword overlap."""

question_terms = {
term.lower().strip(".,?!:;()[]{}")
for term in question.split()
if len(term) > 3
}

chunk_lower = chunk.lower()
 score = 0

for term in question_terms:
if term in chunk_lower:
score += 1

return score

def retrieve_chunks(question: str, chunks: list[str], top_k: int = 4) -> list[str]:

"""Retrieve top chunks using simple keyword scoring."""

if not question.strip():
 raise ValueError("Question cannot be empty.")

scored = [
(score_chunk(question, chunk), chunk)
for chunk in chunks
]

scored.sort(key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True)

selected = [
chunk for score, chunk in scored[:top_k]
if score > 0
]

if not selected and chunks:
selected = chunks[:1]

return selected

def format_context(chunks: list[str]) -> str:

"""Format retrieved chunks for the model."""

if not chunks:
return "No relevant document context found."

blocks = []

for index, chunk in enumerate(chunks, start=1):
blocks.append(f"[Context {index}]\n{chunk}")

return "\n\n".join(blocks)

12.11 File: evaluation.py

This file provides a simple self-check for generated outputs.

"""
Simple evaluation helpers for the capstone assistant.
"""

PROHIBITED_PHRASES = [
"i guarantee",
"100% accurate",
"definitely legal",
"no risk",
"you do not need a professional",
]

def find_prohibited_phrases(text: str) -> list[str]:

"""Find risky phrases in output."""

lowered = text.lower()

return [phrase for phrase in PROHIBITED_PHRASES if phrase in lowered]

def output_self_check(text: str) -> dict:

"""Run a simple output self-check."""

issues = []

if not text.strip():
issues.append("empty_output")

if len(text) > 5000:
issues.append("very_long_output")

prohibited = find_prohibited_phrases(text)

for phrase in prohibited:
issues.append(f"prohibited_phrase:{phrase}")

return {

"passed": len(issues) == 0,
"issues": issues,
}

def format_self_check(result: dict) -> str:

"""Format self-check results."""

if result["passed"]:
return "Self-check passed. No obvious issues detected."

return "Self-check issues:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {issue}" for issue in result["issues"])

12.12 File: app.py

This is the main Streamlit app.

"""
Capstone Project: Personal AI Work Assistant

Run locally:
streamlit run app.py
"""

import streamlit as st

from llm_client import LLMClient from guardrails import assess_request, review_message from memory_store import add_memory, list_memory, clear_memory, format_memory_for_prompt from tools import calculator, create_task_plan from rag_utils import (

extract_text_from_pdf_bytes,
chunk_text,
retrieve_chunks,
format_context,
)

from evaluation import output_self_check, format_self_check

APP_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are a careful personal AI work assistant.

Rules:
- Be clear, practical, and concise.
- Do not invent facts.
- Do not claim that you performed external actions.
- Do not provide legal, medical, financial, or tax conclusions.
- If information is missing, say what is missing.
- For important output, remind the user to review before using.
"""

def call_assistant(user_request: str, extra_context: str = "") -> str:

"""Call the LLM with guardrails and memory context."""

assessment = assess_request(user_request)

if not assessment.allowed:
return f"""
Request blocked.

{review_message(assessment)}

""".strip()

memory_context = format_memory_for_prompt()

prompt = f"""
Saved memory:

{memory_context}

Extra context:

{extra_context or "No extra context."}

User request:

{user_request}

Risk note:

{review_message(assessment) if assessment.needs_review else "No special risk note."}

Respond safely and helpfully.
"""

client = LLMClient()
 answer = client.complete(
 system=APP_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
 user=prompt,
 )

check = output_self_check(answer)

if assessment.needs_review or not check["passed"]:
return f"""

{answer}

---

Review Notice:

{review_message(assessment)}

Output Self-Check:

{format_self_check(check)}

""".strip()

return answer

def render_sidebar() -> None:

"""Render sidebar information."""

st.sidebar.title("Agentic AI With Python")
st.sidebar.caption("Personal AI Work Assistant")

st.sidebar.markdown(
"""
**Modes**
- General assistant
- Document Q&A
- Tools
- Memory
- Evaluation
"""
)

st.sidebar.warning(
"This is a learning project. Review important AI output before using it."
)

def general_assistant_mode() -> None:

"""General assistant mode."""

st.header("General Assistant")

user_request = st.text_area(
"Ask a work, study, or Python AI question:",
height=160,
placeholder="Example: Explain how RAG and tool calling work together.",
)

if st.button("Ask Assistant"):
if not user_request.strip():
st.error("Please enter a request.")
return

with st.spinner("Thinking..."):
try:
answer = call_assistant(user_request)
st.markdown(answer)
except Exception as error:
st.error(f"Something went wrong: {error}")

def document_qa_mode() -> None:

"""Document Q&A mode."""

st.header("Document Q&A")

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader(
"Upload a PDF document",
type=["pdf"],
)

question = st.text_input(
"Ask a question about the document:",
placeholder="Example: What are the key points?",
)

if st.button("Ask Document"):
if uploaded_file is None:
st.error("Please upload a PDF.")
return

if not question.strip():
st.error("Please enter a question.")
return

with st.spinner("Reading and searching document..."):
 try:
 file_bytes = uploaded_file.getvalue()
 text = extract_text_from_pdf_bytes(file_bytes)
 chunks = chunk_text(text)
 selected = retrieve_chunks(question, chunks)
 context = format_context(selected)

rag_prompt = f"""
Answer the question using only the document context.

If the answer is not in the context, say:
"I could not find that in the document."

Document context:

{context}

Question:

{question}

"""

answer = call_assistant(
user_request=rag_prompt,
extra_context="Document Q&A mode is active.",
)

st.markdown(answer)

with st.expander("Retrieved context"):
st.text(context)

except Exception as error:
st.error(f"Document Q&A error: {error}")

def tools_mode() -> None:

"""Tools mode."""

st.header("Tools")

tool_choice = st.selectbox(
"Choose a tool",
["Calculator", "Task Planner"],
)

if tool_choice == "Calculator":
expression = st.text_input(
"Enter arithmetic expression:",
placeholder="Example: (25 * 4) + 10",
)

if st.button("Calculate"):
st.code(calculator(expression))

if tool_choice == "Task Planner":
goal = st.text_area(
"Enter a goal:",
placeholder="Example: Build a PDF chatbot portfolio project.",
)

if st.button("Create Task Plan"):
st.markdown(create_task_plan(goal))

def memory_mode() -> None:

"""Memory mode."""

st.header("Memory")

st.info(
"Memory is stored locally for this demo. Do not save secrets, passwords, API keys, or sensitive personal data."
)

memory_text = st.text_input(
"Add memory:",
placeholder="Example: I prefer concise bullet-point explanations.",
)

if st.button("Remember"):
try:
assessment = assess_request(memory_text)

if not assessment.allowed or "possible_secret" in assessment.categories:
st.error("This memory appears unsafe to save.")
st.text(review_message(assessment))
else:
item = add_memory(memory_text)
st.success(f"Saved memory {item.id}.")
except Exception as error:
st.error(f"Memory error: {error}")

st.subheader("Saved Memory")

memories = list_memory()

if not memories:
st.write("No saved memory.")
else:
for item in memories:
st.write(f"{item.id}. {item.text}")

if st.button("Clear All Memory"):
clear_memory()
st.success("Memory cleared. Refresh to update the display.")

def evaluation_mode() -> None:

"""Simple output evaluation mode."""

st.header("Evaluation Self-Check")

text = st.text_area(
"Paste an AI output to check:",
height=180,
placeholder="Paste generated output here.",
)

if st.button("Run Self-Check"):
result = output_self_check(text)
st.markdown(format_self_check(result))

if result["passed"]:
st.success("No obvious issues detected.")
else:
st.warning("Review recommended.")

def main() -> None:

"""Run the Streamlit app."""

st.set_page_config(
page_title="Personal AI Work Assistant",
page_icon="🤖",
layout="wide",
)

render_sidebar()

st.title("Personal AI Work Assistant")
st.caption("Capstone project for Agentic AI With Python")

mode = st.tabs(
[
"General Assistant",
"Document Q&A",
"Tools",
"Memory",
"Evaluation",
]
)

with mode[0]:
general_assistant_mode()

with mode[1]:
document_qa_mode()

with mode[2]:
tools_mode()

with mode[3]:
memory_mode()

with mode[4]:
evaluation_mode()

12.18 How the Capstone App Works

The app has five main modes.

Mode 1: General Assistant

The user asks a normal question.

The app:

User request
↓
Guardrail check
↓
Memory context
↓
LLM response
↓
Output self-check
↓
Final answer

Mode 2: Document Q&A

The user uploads a PDF and asks a question.

The app:

PDF upload
↓
Extract text
↓
Chunk text
↓
Retrieve relevant chunks
↓
Ask LLM using context
↓
Show answer and retrieved context

This is a lightweight RAG pattern.

Mode 3: Tools

The user can use:

  • Calculator
  • Task planner

These tools use normal Python logic.

Not every feature needs an LLM.

Mode 4: Memory

The user can save memory such as:

I prefer concise explanations.

The app uses memory in future assistant prompts.

The app warns users not to store secrets or sensitive data.

Mode 5: Evaluation

The user can paste output and run a basic self-check.

The self-check looks for:

  • Empty output
  • Very long output
  • Risky phrases
  • Unsupported certainty

12.23 Secrets in Deployment

Never hardcode API keys.

Bad:

api_key = "sk-your-real-key"

Better:

api_key = read_secret("OPENAI_API_KEY")

Your repository should include:

.streamlit/secrets.toml.example

but not:

.streamlit/secrets.toml

That is why .gitignore includes:

.streamlit/secrets.toml

Secrets should be configured through your deployment platform’s secure settings.

12.24 Deployment Mistakes to Avoid

Mistake 1: Committing Secrets

Never commit API keys.

Check your repository before pushing.

Mistake 2: Missing requirements.txt

If dependencies are missing, the deployed app may fail to build.

Mistake 3: Using Local File Paths

A path that works on your laptop may not work in the cloud.

Use uploaded files or platform-supported storage.

Mistake 4: Assuming Local Memory Persists

Some hosting environments may reset local files.

For production memory, use a real database.

Mistake 5: No README

A project without setup instructions is harder to trust.

Mistake 6: No Limitations Section

A serious AI project explains what it cannot do.

Mistake 7: No Human Review Warning

AI output should be reviewed before important use.

Mistake 8: No Error Handling

Users should see helpful errors, not stack traces.
